question.text: What common pattern emerges from SEBI enforcement cases related to AML non-compliance by stock brokers?

answer.text: Brokers often fail to implement AML mechanisms, classify client risk properly, monitor transactions, analyze alerts/STRs, and maintain written records
Brokers typically charge excessive brokerage fees leading to AML violations
Brokers usually have too many compliance officers which creates confusion
Brokers generally fail because they implement too many AML checks, causing customer complaints

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI enforcement cases against brokers reveal recurring failures: not implementing AML mechanisms, not classifying client risk properly, not monitoring transactions, failing to analyze alerts/STRs, and not maintaining written records. The Trap: Excessive AML checks or too many compliance officers are not the real issue — the documented pattern is too little compliance, not too much. Note: The recurring themes from the source are KYC/risk-categorization, transaction monitoring, STR/alert analysis, and record-keeping failures.
